summary: Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. from Yale University by 1990. She held law faculty positions at CU Boulder and the University at Buffalo.
Rebecca Sundén works in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin, attested in 2026.

Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under numerous academic and traditional teachers. He held teaching posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1948 to 1952 and served as a professor there from circa 1974 to 1999.
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He taught at Komazawa University from circa 1935 to 1973.

Reiko Ohnuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at UC Berkeley and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez. She held posts at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa (~1924–1927). His career included professorships at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia and Kyoto Women's University, as well as an emeritus post at Ryukoku University.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at Freie Universität Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1826–1831), where he served as an assistant professor (1832) and later as an außerordentlicher Professor (1849–1870).

Reinhold Niebuhr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School (~1913–1915), and held a post at Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena. He taught at St Augustine's College and served as head librarian of the India Office Library from 1869 to 1893.
Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College from circa 1958 to 1968.

Reita Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Toyo University (attested 2015). Affiliations attested in 2015 include positions at Toyo University and the Shinshu Otani-ha Shinran Buddhist Center.
Remeen Firoz is a researcher in Indology who is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron.

Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff. She is attested in 2026 as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Renda Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who received traditional training under Kai Zhi, Shengfa, and Kai Tong.
Renjo Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1969–1975) and later held a post there from circa 1975 to 2014.

René Grousset studied at the University of Montpellier and worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He held posts at the Musée Guimet, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, and the Louvre Museum.
